title: Nonexistent tool name reports 'not in the active tool set' instead of 'unknown tool', implying access control rather than a typo/hallucinated name
observed: Calling a tool name the model made up ('frobnicate', never registered anywhere) shows: 'frobnicate ─── auto-approved · 0.0s / Frobnicate / → tool "frobnicate" is not available to this agent: it is not in the active tool set' (01-waitfor-timeout-line9.txt, after WAITFOR /unknown tool/ timed out because that text never appears).
expected: The 'unknown tool %q' error path (internal/harness/turn.go:681) exists specifically for this case but is unreachable for a real CLI session: toolActive() (turn.go:782-791) returns true only when the lane's ActiveToolNames is empty, and a real session's ActiveToolNames is always the CLI's populated tool list, so any unregistered name is rejected by the 'not in the active tool set' branch (turn.go:667) first. The two messages read very differently to a user — one implies a permissions restriction, the other a nonexistent/mistyped tool — and only the misleading one is ever reachable in practice.
design_ref: internal/harness/turn.go:657-681 (beginTool's toolActive check at 657 short-circuits before the registry lookup at 673-681); turn.go:782-791 toolActive
